objects.description: Core task object representing a scheduled unit of work with interval, iterations, optional callbacks, and coordination via StatusRequest. Provides enable/disable, timing, and lifecycle control. Used with Scheduler chains.
Scheduler that manages a doubly-linked chain of Task objects and executes them cooperatively according to timing rules. Supports priorities, sleep, thread-safe request processing, and timing stats.
Bit-packed internal state flags for a Task (enabled, in OnEnable, canceled, optional self-destruct, waiting mode, timeout flag). Used inside Task.
Callback type used by Task for main execution function. Either std::function<void()> or plain function pointer based on compile-time option.
Callback type invoked when a Task is disabled. Signature void().
Callback type invoked on Task enable to approve enabling. Returns bool.

functions.name: _task_enqueue_request
functions.description: Weak hook used by _TASK_THREAD_SAFE to enqueue a task/scheduler action request into a platform-provided queue. The scheduler calls this to post requests that will be processed in Scheduler::processRequests(). Default weak implementation returns false.
requirements: Only available/used when compiled with _TASK_THREAD_SAFE.
Caller must pass a valid non-null pointer to a _task_request_t structure that remains valid until dequeued and processed.
Return value indicates whether the request was successfully queued (true) or not (false).
Must be implemented by the target platform to enable thread-safe requests.

functions.name: _task_dequeue_request
functions.description: Weak hook used by _TASK_THREAD_SAFE to dequeue the next pending action request from a platform-provided queue into req. Scheduler::processRequests() repeatedly calls this until it returns false.
requirements: Only available/used when compiled with _TASK_THREAD_SAFE.
Caller must pass a valid non-null pointer to a writable _task_request_t structure to receive the dequeued request.
Returns true if a request was dequeued and stored into req; false when the queue is empty.
Must be implemented by the target platform together with _task_enqueue_request to enable thread-safe requests.

functions.name: _task_micros
functions.description: Internal wrapper for platform time in microseconds. On Arduino builds maps to micros(); in non-Arduino builds it must be provided by the target (declaration only here). Used for high-resolution timing, sleep bookkeeping, and _TASK_TIMECRITICAL metrics.
requirements: When _TASK_NON_ARDUINO is not defined and (a) _TASK_MICRO_RES is enabled or (b) _TASK_SLEEP_ON_IDLE_RUN or _TASK_TIMECRITICAL are enabled, this function is defined and callable.
When _TASK_NON_ARDUINO is defined, the application/platform must provide an implementation with the same signature.
Must be callable from interrupt context on platforms where it is used in IRAM or time-critical sections.

functions.name: _task_millis
functions.description: Internal wrapper for platform time in milliseconds. On Arduino builds maps to millis(); on non-Arduino builds must be provided by the target. Used for all core scheduling timestamps and delay calculations (unless microsecond resolution is enabled).
requirements: When _TASK_NON_ARDUINO is not defined and _TASK_MICRO_RES is not enabled, this function is defined and callable.
When _TASK_NON_ARDUINO is defined, the application/platform must provide an implementation with the same signature.
Should be monotonic and handle rollover naturally (library code is rollover-safe).

functions.name: _task_yield
functions.description: Internal wrapper for yielding to the platform runtime. On Arduino builds maps to yield() unless _TASK_DO_NOT_YIELD is defined. Used by Scheduler::execute() between task checks.
requirements: Available only when _TASK_DO_NOT_YIELD is not defined.
When _TASK_NON_ARDUINO is defined, the target must provide an implementation with the same signature.
Should be safe to call frequently from the main scheduling loop.

functions.name: Task::Task
functions.signature: Task::Task(unsigned long aInterval=0, long aIterations=0, Scheduler* aScheduler=NULL, bool aEnable=false, bool aSelfDestruct=false)
functions.description: Constructor (OO callbacks mode) creating a task with interval and iteration count, optionally attaching it to a scheduler and enabling it immediately. In OO mode, task logic is provided by overriding virtual methods.
requirements: This overload exists only when compiled with _TASK_OO_CALLBACKS.
If aScheduler is non-null, it must be a valid Scheduler instance; the task will be added to its chain.
If aEnable is true, OnEnable() will be called; it must return true for the task to become enabled.
If _TASK_SELF_DESTRUCT is enabled and aSelfDestruct is true, the task may request self-destruction on disable.

functions.name: Task::~Task
functions.description: Destructor that ensures the task is disabled and removed from its scheduler chain before deletion.
requirements: If the task is enabled at destruction time, disable() is invoked which may call OnDisable.
If the task belongs to a Scheduler (iScheduler non-null), it will be deleted from that scheduler.
Do not destroy a Task while it is executing inside its callback to avoid undefined behavior.

functions.name: StatusRequest::StatusRequest
functions.description: Constructs a StatusRequest object in completed state (count=0, status=0). Initializes timeout fields when _TASK_TIMEOUT is enabled.
requirements: No parameters; object is ready to be used for signaling/waiting.
When _TASK_TIMEOUT is enabled, timeout and start time are initialized to 0.

functions.name: StatusRequest::setWaiting
functions.description: Activates the StatusRequest by setting the number of outstanding signals to wait for and clearing the status code. Starts the timeout counter when enabled.
requirements: aCount must be the number of events to wait for; must fit in unsigned int.
When _TASK_TIMEOUT is enabled, this resets iStarttime to current time.

functions.name: StatusRequest::isPending
functions.description: Returns true if there are outstanding events to wait for (iCount != 0).
requirements: No special requirements.

functions.name: StatusRequest::isCompleted
functions.description: Returns true if all events have completed (iCount == 0).
requirements: No special requirements.

functions.name: StatusRequest::getStatus
functions.description: Returns the last status code that was signaled to this request. Negative indicates error, 0 OK, positive OK with code.
requirements: Only meaningful after at least one signal() or signalComplete().

functions.name: StatusRequest::getCount
functions.description: Returns remaining number of signals required before completion.
requirements: No special requirements.

functions.name: Task::getStatusRequest
functions.description: Returns the pointer to the external StatusRequest associated with this task (used for other tasks to wait on this task).
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_STATUS_REQUEST.
May return nullptr if none is set.

functions.name: Task::getInternalStatusRequest
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the task's internal StatusRequest used by the scheduler to indicate task completion/cancellation/abort.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_STATUS_REQUEST.

functions.name: StatusRequest::signal
functions.description: Signals completion of one pending event and sets the status code. If aStatus is negative, completes the StatusRequest immediately (iCount->0). Returns true if the request is now complete.
requirements: If already completed (iCount==0), the call is ignored and current status unchanged.
Increments are not allowed; only decrements one (if iCount > 0).
Callable from ISR if placed in IRAM on supported ESP chips when _TASK_ISR_SUPPORT is enabled.

functions.name: StatusRequest::signalComplete
functions.description: Completes the StatusRequest immediately regardless of remaining count, setting the status code to aStatus.
requirements: If already completed (iCount==0), the call is ignored.
Callable from ISR if placed in IRAM on supported ESP chips when _TASK_ISR_SUPPORT is enabled.

functions.name: Task::waitFor
functions.signature: bool Task::waitFor(StatusRequest* aStatusRequest, unsigned long aInterval=0, long aIterations=1)
functions.description: Configures the task to wait on a StatusRequest until it completes. Optionally sets new interval and iteration count, then enables the task to run when the request completes (no delay on completion).
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_STATUS_REQUEST.
aStatusRequest must be a valid non-null pointer; if null the call has no effect and returns false.
Sets iStatus.waiting to internal node-lay mode; task will start immediately upon completion and be rescheduled from that point.
If aInterval is provided, it becomes the task interval; aIterations sets remaining iterations.

functions.name: Task::waitForDelayed
functions.signature: bool Task::waitForDelayed(StatusRequest* aStatusRequest, unsigned long aInterval=0, long aIterations=1)
functions.description: Configures the task to wait on a StatusRequest until it completes, then starts after a delay equal to the current interval (or provided aInterval).
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_STATUS_REQUEST.
aStatusRequest must be a valid non-null pointer; if null the call returns false.
If aInterval is non-zero, updates the task interval; aIterations sets remaining iterations.
Sets iStatus.waiting to delayed mode; schedules first run after completion plus interval.

functions.name: StatusRequest::resetTimeout
functions.description: Resets the internal timeout timer to current time for this StatusRequest.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_TIMEOUT.
Has effect only when a non-zero timeout has been configured via setTimeout().

functions.name: StatusRequest::untilTimeout
functions.description: Returns remaining time until the configured timeout expires, or -1 if no timeout is configured.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_TIMEOUT.
Return value may be negative if timeout already elapsed.

functions.name: Task::isEnabled
functions.description: Returns whether the task is currently enabled for scheduling/execution.
requirements: No special requirements.

functions.name: Task::getInterval
functions.description: Returns the current execution interval for the task (ms by default or µs if _TASK_MICRO_RES).
requirements: No special requirements.

functions.name: Task::getIterations
functions.description: Returns remaining iteration count (0 means last iteration is due next; -1 means run forever).
requirements: No special requirements.

functions.name: Task::getRunCounter
functions.description: Returns how many times the task callback has been invoked since last enable(). First run is counted as 1.
requirements: No special requirements.

functions.name: Task::OnEnable
functions.description: Virtual lifecycle callback (OO mode) invoked by enable(). Default implementation returns true to allow enabling.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_OO_CALLBACKS.
Override in derived classes to perform initialization; return true to enable, false to keep disabled.
Should be fast and non-blocking.

functions.name: Task::OnDisable
functions.description: Virtual lifecycle callback (OO mode) invoked when task is being disabled and was previously enabled. Default implementation is no-op.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_OO_CALLBACKS.
Override in derived classes to perform cleanup; must not delete the task unless designed for self-destruction.

functions.name: Task::setCallback
functions.description: Assigns or replaces the task main callback function (function-pointer mode).
requirements: Available only when NOT compiled with _TASK_OO_CALLBACKS.
aCallback should be a fast, non-blocking function; may be nullptr (task will be skipped when scheduled).

functions.name: Task::setOnEnable
functions.description: Sets or replaces the OnEnable callback (function-pointer mode) used when enabling the task to decide activation.
requirements: Available only when NOT compiled with _TASK_OO_CALLBACKS.
aCallback signature must be bool(). May be nullptr to remove hook.
Should be fast and non-blocking.

functions.name: Task::setOnDisable
functions.description: Sets or replaces the OnDisable callback (function-pointer mode) invoked when a previously-enabled task is disabled.
requirements: Available only when NOT compiled with _TASK_OO_CALLBACKS.
aCallback signature must be void(). May be nullptr to remove hook.
Should be fast and non-blocking.

functions.name: Task::reset
functions.description: Initializes the task to default state: disabled, cleared flags, zeroed timing fields, detaches from scheduler, resets counters, clears status request and timeout fields where applicable.
requirements: Internal method; typically called by constructors. Safe to call only when task is not in use by a scheduler.

functions.name: Task::set
functions.signature: void Task::set(unsigned long aInterval, long aIterations)
functions.description: Sets execution parameters (interval and iterations) for OO-callbacks mode. Also delays the task by the new interval.
requirements: Available only when _TASK_OO_CALLBACKS is enabled.
Does not enable the task; use enable()/restart() to activate.
aIterations may be -1 for infinite.

functions.name: Task::setIterations
functions.description: Sets the remaining iteration count and stores it for potential restarts.
requirements: Does not enable the task; to re-run use restart()/restartDelayed().

functions.name: Task::yield
functions.description: Switches the task to a new callback for the next scheduling step and forces immediate rescheduling (splits work across passes). Adjusts run counter and iterations to treat the yielded part as the same logical run.
requirements: Available only when NOT compiled with _TASK_OO_CALLBACKS.
aCallback must be non-null and non-blocking.
Task must be enabled to take effect on next execute() pass.

functions.name: Task::yieldOnce
functions.description: Switches to a new callback for exactly one subsequent execution, then automatically sets iterations to 1 so the task will disable after that run.
requirements: Available only when NOT compiled with _TASK_OO_CALLBACKS.
aCallback must be non-null and non-blocking.

functions.name: Task::enable
functions.description: Enables the task, invoking OnEnable/enable hook if present, resets run counter and scheduling so the task is ready to run as soon as possible. Initializes/reset timeout and internal status request state.
requirements: Task must belong to a Scheduler (added via addTask) or enabling will fail (returns false).
OnEnable (if set or overridden) is invoked every call; it must return true to enable.
Callable from ISR on supported ESP chips if _TASK_ISR_SUPPORT is enabled.

functions.name: Task::enableIfNot
functions.description: Enables the task only if it is currently disabled. Returns true if it was already enabled; false if it was disabled and is now enabled.
requirements: Task should belong to a Scheduler; otherwise enableIfNot() will fail to enable.
Callable from ISR on supported ESP chips if _TASK_ISR_SUPPORT is enabled.

functions.name: Task::enableDelayed
functions.description: Enables the task (invoking enable()) then applies an initial delay before its first run.
requirements: Task should belong to a Scheduler; otherwise enabling will fail.
aDelay is in time units matching build resolution (ms or µs).
Callable from ISR on supported ESP chips if _TASK_ISR_SUPPORT is enabled.

functions.name: Task::setTimeout
functions.signature: void Task::setTimeout(unsigned long aTimeout, bool aReset=false)
functions.description: Sets an overall timeout for the task. Optionally resets the timeout start counter immediately.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_TIMEOUT.
aTimeout == 0 disables timeout.
If aReset is true, internal start time is set to current time.

functions.name: Task::resetTimeout
functions.description: Resets the task's overall timeout start time and clears the timed-out flag.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_TIMEOUT.

functions.name: Task::getTimeout
functions.description: Returns the configured task timeout period.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_TIMEOUT.

functions.name: Task::untilTimeout
functions.description: Returns remaining time until the task's overall timeout occurs, or -1 if no timeout is set.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_TIMEOUT.
Return value may be negative if timeout already elapsed.

functions.name: Task::isTimedOut
functions.description: Returns whether the task has timed out (set internally by the scheduler when timeout is detected).
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_TIMEOUT.

functions.name: Task::delay
functions.description: Delays the next execution of the task by aDelay (or by the current interval if aDelay==0). Leaves enable state unchanged.
requirements: Callable while enabled or disabled; affects scheduling baseline only if enabled.
Callable from ISR on supported ESP chips if _TASK_ISR_SUPPORT is enabled.

functions.name: Task::adjust
functions.description: Adjusts the task schedule by shifting the next run time. Negative values pull the schedule closer (earlier), positive values push it later.
requirements: Has no effect if aInterval==0.
For positive adjustments, modifies internal delay; for negative, moves previous timestamp backward.

functions.name: Task::forceNextIteration
functions.description: Forces the next iteration to be eligible immediately on the next scheduler pass and shifts the schedule from that moment onward.
requirements: Task should be enabled for an immediate run to occur on the next pass.
Callable from ISR on supported ESP chips if _TASK_ISR_SUPPORT is enabled.

functions.name: Task::setInterval
functions.description: Sets the execution interval and delays the task by the same value (next run after the new interval).
requirements: Does not enable the task.
To run immediately with a new interval, call forceNextIteration() after this call or use setIntervalNodelay().

functions.name: Task::setIntervalNodelay
functions.signature: void Task::setIntervalNodelay(unsigned long aInterval, unsigned int aOption)
functions.description: Sets the interval without necessarily delaying the task. Behavior depends on aOption: KEEP (preserve timing if possible), RECALC (proportionally adjust delay), RESET (reset schedule from now).
requirements: aOption must be one of TASK_INTERVAL_KEEP, TASK_INTERVAL_RECALC, TASK_INTERVAL_RESET.
Does not enable the task.

functions.name: Task::disable
functions.description: Disables the task. If it was enabled, invokes OnDisable/disable hook. Signals internal StatusRequest completion and may request self-destruction if configured.
requirements: Returns previous enabled state (true if it was enabled).
Callable from ISR on supported ESP chips if _TASK_ISR_SUPPORT is enabled.
OnDisable is called only if task was previously enabled.

functions.name: Task::abort
functions.description: Stops task execution immediately, marks as canceled/aborted, does not invoke OnDisable, and completes internal StatusRequest with TASK_SR_ABORT. May request self-destruction if configured.
requirements: Callable from ISR on supported ESP chips if _TASK_ISR_SUPPORT is enabled.

functions.name: Task::cancel
functions.description: Marks task as canceled then disables it (thereby invoking OnDisable if previously enabled). Completes internal StatusRequest with TASK_SR_ABORT before disabling.
requirements: Callable from ISR on supported ESP chips if _TASK_ISR_SUPPORT is enabled.

functions.name: Task::isCanceled
functions.description: Returns whether the task has been canceled (set by cancel() or abort()).
requirements: No special requirements.

functions.name: Task::restart
functions.description: Resets remaining iterations to the last configured value and enables the task immediately.
requirements: Callable from ISR on supported ESP chips if _TASK_ISR_SUPPORT is enabled.
Task must belong to a Scheduler to enable.

functions.name: Task::restartDelayed
functions.description: Resets remaining iterations to the last configured value and enables the task with an initial delay before the first run.
requirements: Callable from ISR on supported ESP chips if _TASK_ISR_SUPPORT is enabled.
Task must belong to a Scheduler to enable.

functions.name: Task::isFirstIteration
functions.description: Returns true on or before the first actual callback invocation after enabling (iRunCounter <= 1).
requirements: No special requirements.

functions.name: Task::isLastIteration
functions.description: Returns true when remaining iterations count is 0 (i.e., the current pass is the last for finite-iteration tasks).
requirements: Meaningful only for tasks with finite iterations (>=0).

functions.name: Task::getOverrun
functions.description: Returns the computed overrun value (microseconds) for the last run: (scheduled finish - actual time). Negative means behind schedule.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_TIMECRITICAL.

functions.name: Task::getStartDelay
functions.description: Returns the start delay (microseconds) for the last run: time between scheduled start and actual start.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_TIMECRITICAL.

functions.name: Task::setId
functions.description: Sets the task ID used for WDT/debug identification.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_WDT_IDS.
aID should be within the application's chosen ID range.

functions.name: Task::getId
functions.description: Returns the task ID assigned for WDT/debug identification.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_WDT_IDS.

functions.name: Task::setControlPoint
functions.description: Sets the current control point marker within the task callback for watchdog/logging.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_WDT_IDS.
Application defines semantics of control points.

functions.name: Task::getControlPoint
functions.description: Returns the current/last set control point value.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_WDT_IDS.

functions.name: Task::setLtsPointer
functions.description: Stores a Local Task Storage pointer for this task for user-defined persistent per-task data.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_LTS_POINTER.
Caller is responsible for the lifetime and type-safety of the pointed data.

functions.name: Task::getLtsPointer
functions.description: Returns the Local Task Storage pointer previously set for this task (or nullptr).
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_LTS_POINTER.

functions.name: Scheduler::Scheduler
functions.description: Constructs a Scheduler and initializes its internal state and task chain. If sleep support is enabled, installs default sleep method.
requirements: Safe to instantiate multiple schedulers; can be linked in priority layers via setHighPriorityScheduler() when enabled.

functions.name: Scheduler::init
functions.description: Initializes internal variables, task chain pointers, paused/enabled flags, sleep and timecritical counters, and marks scheduler enabled.
requirements: Normally called by constructor; may be called to reinitialize an instance with an empty chain.

functions.name: Scheduler::addTask
functions.description: Appends a Task to the end of this scheduler's execution chain if it is not already assigned to any scheduler.
requirements: aTask must not already belong to any scheduler (aTask.iScheduler must be NULL), otherwise the call returns without effect.
The scheduler temporarily disables itself during mutation; do not call concurrently from other contexts without _TASK_THREAD_SAFE routing.

functions.name: Scheduler::deleteTask
functions.description: Removes a Task from this scheduler's chain if it belongs to this scheduler. Relinks surrounding tasks accordingly.
requirements: Only removes the task if aTask.iScheduler == this; otherwise returns without effect.
Safe to call for first, middle, or last tasks; clears the task's scheduler and link pointers.

functions.name: Scheduler::disableAll
functions.description: Disables all tasks in this scheduler. Optionally recurses into higher priority scheduler layers to disable them as well.
requirements: This overload is available only when compiled with _TASK_PRIORITY.
If _TASK_SELF_DESTRUCT is enabled, tasks requesting self-destruction may be deleted during traversal; do not keep stale pointers.

functions.name: Scheduler::enableAll
functions.description: Enables all tasks in this scheduler. Optionally recurses into higher priority scheduler layers to enable them as well.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_PRIORITY.

functions.name: Scheduler::setHighPriorityScheduler
functions.description: Sets a higher-priority scheduler to be executed from this scheduler on each pass. Also disables sleep on the higher priority scheduler.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_PRIORITY.
aScheduler must not be this (self) to avoid infinite recursion; self is ignored.
If _TASK_SLEEP_ON_IDLE_RUN is enabled, high-priority scheduler will have sleep disabled.

functions.name: Scheduler::allowSleep
functions.description: Enables or disables entering sleep on idle passes for this scheduler (sleep mode support must be compiled).
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_SLEEP_ON_IDLE_RUN.
A custom SleepMethod can be installed via setSleepMethod().

functions.name: Scheduler::startNow
functions.description: Aligns all enabled tasks' previous time to start from now minus their current delay, effectively scheduling next run at the proper relative time. Optionally applies to higher priority schedulers.
requirements: This overload is available only when compiled with _TASK_PRIORITY.
Should be called typically at the end of setup() to align schedules.

functions.name: Scheduler::timeUntilNextIteration
functions.description: Returns time until aTask is scheduled to run next. Returns 0 if due now/overdue, or -1 if not determinable (disabled or waiting on a pending StatusRequest).
requirements: If _TASK_STATUS_REQUEST is enabled and the task waits on a pending StatusRequest, returns -1.
If the task is disabled, returns -1.

functions.name: Scheduler::currentTask
functions.description: Returns reference to the task currently processed by the scheduler. Deprecated; prefer getCurrentTask().
requirements: Only valid during execution of callbacks or OnEnable/OnDisable hooks within execute() context.

functions.name: Scheduler::getCurrentTask
functions.description: Returns pointer to the task currently processed by the scheduler (or the task being enabled/disabled in hooks).
requirements: Only meaningful during execute()/OnEnable/OnDisable context; may be null otherwise.

functions.name: Scheduler::currentLts
functions.description: Returns Local Task Storage pointer for the currently executing task.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_LTS_POINTER.
Must be called during a task's execution or enable/disable hooks to be valid; may return nullptr.

functions.name: Scheduler::isOverrun
functions.description: Returns true if the current task recorded a negative overrun (i.e., behind schedule) this pass.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_TIMECRITICAL.
Valid only during/after a task execution within execute().

functions.name: Scheduler::cpuLoadReset
functions.description: Resets internal CPU load counters used for timecritical statistics.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_TIMECRITICAL.

functions.name: Scheduler::getCpuLoadTotal
functions.description: Returns elapsed time in microseconds since last cpuLoadReset(). Used as a basis for CPU load calculations.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_TIMECRITICAL.

functions.name: Scheduler::setSleepMethod
functions.description: Installs a custom sleep callback to be used when this scheduler is allowed to sleep on idle passes. Stores global pointers so only one scheduler manages sleep.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_SLEEP_ON_IDLE_RUN.
aCallback must be non-null to take effect.

functions.name: Scheduler::requestAction
functions.description: Enqueues a prebuilt task/scheduler request for thread-safe processing during execute() by calling the platform _task_enqueue_request hook.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_THREAD_SAFE.
aRequest must be a valid non-null pointer to a request structure that remains valid until processed.
Returns true if enqueued successfully.

functions.name: Scheduler::processRequests
functions.description: Dequeues and dispatches queued thread-safe requests by repeatedly calling _task_dequeue_request() and invoking the corresponding methods on target objects.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _TASK_THREAD_SAFE.
Assumes requests were put on the queue by platform hooks; processes until queue empty.
Requests with null object_ptr are ignored.

functions.name: Scheduler::execute
functions.description: Performs one scheduling pass: optionally executes higher priority scheduler, processes thread-safe requests, evaluates and invokes tasks as eligible, manages timeouts, status-request waits, tickless hints, and optional idle sleep. Returns true if no task callbacks were invoked (idle run).
requirements: Should be called frequently (typically from loop()).
Not reentrant; call only from a single thread unless using _TASK_THREAD_SAFE request mechanism for cross-thread control.
Callbacks must be non-blocking to preserve cooperative behavior.
If _TASK_SELF_DESTRUCT is enabled, tasks may be deleted during/after disable; avoid holding raw pointers across passes.

functions.name: SleepMethod
functions.description: Platform-specific idle sleep function used when _TASK_SLEEP_ON_IDLE_RUN is enabled. Implementation varies by architecture (AVR uses IDLE sleep; Teensy uses WFI; ESP8266 uses delay(1) for short durations; ESP32 placeholder; STM32F1 uses WFI; MSP432 uses delay(1); MSP430 uses sleep(1); default is no-op).
requirements: Available and used only when _TASK_SLEEP_ON_IDLE_RUN is enabled and set as the current sleep method (Scheduler::setSleepMethod may override).
aDuration units are microseconds as passed from scheduler (used/ignored depending on platform).
On platforms with not-implemented branches (e.g., ESP32 light sleep commented), current implementation is effectively a no-op.

unharnessable_functions.name: _task_enqueue_request
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires _task_request_t definition and a platform queue implementation; the type is not available in the provided objects and the weak hook may be undefined on this build.

unharnessable_functions.name: _task_dequeue_request
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires _task_request_t definition and a platform queue implementation; the type is not available in the provided objects and the weak hook may be undefined on this build.
